messages.subject: readUnits versus getData
parts:
Hi,
Is there an advantage (e.g. speed) in using readUnits over getData,
other than ease of use? getData or getIntensities seems slower, while
readUnits seems faster for units that I have recently already
accessed. I'm asking because I'm writing a function and I like to have
the intensities returned as one matrix with the groups collapsed. So
its easy to do this by getting the cell indices and then using
getData(this,indices= unlist(cellindices),fields="intensities"). Is
there a built in way to collapse the results from readUnits into a
single matrix (I know I can collapse the group list manually, but if
there is a built in method, then I would trust it more given how
deeply listed the data is).

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] readUnits versus getData
parts:
On 3/1/07, epurdom <epu...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi,
> Is there an advantage (e.g. speed) in using readUnits over getData,
> other than ease of use? getData or getIntensities seems slower, while
> readUnits seems faster for units that I have recently already
> accessed.

Note that you are entering a bit of unsettled API here, so expect some
things to be not perfectly consistent. Don't expect the behavior of
readUnits() in one class to carry over to another class, e.g.
AffymetrixCdfFile, AffymetrixCelSet, ProbeLevelModel, ChipEffectSet
etc.

The general idea is that readUnits(..., units=...) is retrieving data
unit by unit (unit == probeset) structured according to the CDF,
whereas getData(..., indices=...) is retrieving data cell by cell
(cell == probe) without making use of the CDF. So, they are actually
doing quite different things.

> I'm asking because I'm writing a function and I like to have
> the intensities returned as one matrix with the groups collapsed. So
> its easy to do this by getting the cell indices and then using
> getData(this,indices= unlist(cellindices),fields="intensities"). Is
> there a built in way to collapse the results from readUnits into a
> single matrix (I know I can collapse the group list manually, but if
> there is a built in method, then I would trust it more given how
> deeply listed the data is).

If you're asking for a way to return CDF data in a flat table, say:

> cells <- getCellIndicesFlat(cdf, units=101:102)
> cells
unit group cell
101 1 323
101 2 324
101 3 325
101 4 326
102 1 327
...

the answer is that there is *no* such function in aroma.affymetrix yet.
(Ideally this will be implemented in I/O package affxparser.)
However, if you're interested in implementing such a function for
aroma.affymetrix, work from getCellIndices() to get a list structure
which you then flatten/collapse. It is important that such a method
support units with different number of groups, which also makes
everything more tricky and slower.

With that function you could then do,

> y <- getData(this, indices=cells$cell, fields=c("intensities", "stdvs"))
> str(y)
'data.frame': 8 obs. of 2 variables:
$ intensities: num 1224 747 1928 1743 345 ...
$ stdvs : num 1.02 1.02 1.01 1.02 1.07 ...

and merge it with the above to get:

> data <- cbind(cells, y)
> data
unit group cell intensities stdvs
1 1 323 1224 1.02
1 2 324 747 1.02
1 3 325 1928 1.01
1 4 326 1743 1.02
2 1 502 345 1.07
...

Is this what you are trying to do? The following might be enough for
you right now?

flattenCellIndices <- function(cells, ...) {
# Flatten cell data
cells <- unlist(cells);

# Do some tricks to clean up the names
names(cells) <- gsub("[.](groups|indices)", "", names(cells));

# Extract the vector of unit names
unitNames <- gsub("[.].*", "", names(cells))

# Extract the unit group names
groupNames <- gsub(".*[.]", "", names(cells))

# Merge data
data.frame(unitNames=unitNames, groupNames=groupNames, cell=cells)
} # flattenCellIndices()


Example:

> cells <- getCellIndices(cdf, units=101:102)
> flattenCellIndices(cells)
unitNames groupNames cell
1 SNP_A-4192675 A 323
2 SNP_A-4192675 G 324
3 SNP_A-4192675 A 325
4 SNP_A-4192675 G 326
5 SNP_A-1783398 A 327
6 SNP_A-1783398 G 328
7 SNP_A-1783398 A 329
8 SNP_A-1783398 G 330

Hope this helps a bit
